items.title: Show HN: Ramasite, a Self-Contained Laravel/Filament/SQLite CMS
items.titleZh: Show HN：Ramasite，一个独立的 Laravel/Filament/SQLite CMS
items.summary:
I'm new here, and little nervous about posting, but here goes. I'm not a newbie. I started programming in BASIC when my dad bought home a TRS-80 Model I in 1980, when I was 16. Other than a 9-year stint as active duty military, I've spent 46 years either personally or professionally working in tech. I've programmed in RPG using punch cards for an IBM /System360, and COBOL on a DEC pdp 11/34. I've worked professionally with VB, C#, SQL Server, ColdFusion, PHP, and more. I've seen a lot of technologies come and go. So this ain't the first time I've jogged around this track. Here's the problem I wanted to solve: I hate WordPress. I mean, as a concept, it's fine, but I used to have a fairly popular motorcycle blog on WP that got trashed by hackers. I've also run into that problem with customers. When hackers find a wordpress site, they just bang on it like a drum. It's a pain. It's also a pain just to manage it, with a wild-west plugin system where plugins constantly fall in and out of compatibility. I'm also not a huge fan of PHP, but since it comes stock with pretty much every shared hosting service, where a lot of my web work is done, it's kind of the default for doing web stuff. Back in about 2006 or so, I built my own blogging software, which I called .Blog, as an ASP.NET deal in C#. It took me about 6 months to build, start to finish. I didn't have time to keep up with it, which is why I defaulted back to WP sometime around 2014. I migrated to Grav when I ran across it (I guess around 2020 or so), and I liked that. But Grav ran into some issues, and development on it really slowed. In the past year or so, the company I work for has been delving into using Claude Code, and I got an idea. What if I could just use Claude Code to build a CMS that has everything I want, and nothing I don't? This project is the result of that idea. I designed the specifications for what I wanted it to do, and let Claude Code handle the actual code writing. I started with a flat-file, markdown-based flat-file CMS, and iterated on that. Fiddling around with markdown files and folders started to get tedious, so I moved towards SQLite as the back-end, to create a system as self-contained and easy to use as possible. This project is, I think, the final result of that idea. This project, from start to finish, took about 2 weeks to build using Laravel/Filament/PHP with Claude Code, compared to the 6 months it took to build .Blog by hand, 20 years ago. Cripes, I'm old. Personally, I'm pretty pleased with how this project turned out. I'm running two public websites on it. I'd be interested to hear what others think.

items.title: Show HN: Yogurt – Free, private, open-source alternative to Granola
items.titleZh: Show HN：酸奶——格兰诺拉麦片的免费、私有、开源替代品
items.summary:
Hey HN, I’m Eric and I want to share an OSS project that I’ve been building in my free time. Yogurt is a free, MIT licensed desktop app that uses on-device AI models to transcribe, summarize, and chat with your meetings. Here's a quick demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BFfbXAwRq98 Similar to Granola, Yogurt runs in the background and does not join your calls. But unlike Granola, Yogurt is open-source, free to use, and private. Your meeting transcripts, call recordings, and summaries never leave your computer. As small OSS models have gotten faster and more powerful, Yogurt seemed like a pretty obvious win for privacy and cost conscious folks. You do not need a frontier model to summarize meeting notes or answer questions about them. And if you want to make your notes available to a frontier model, you can just share it with Anthropic, OpenAI, etc. directly via Yogurt’s local MCP server. There’s no need to use a paid cloud service as a middleman. I tried some of the most popular OSS note taking tools, and most were missing features like calendar integration, MCP server, etc. or required you to connect or create an account. And more than that, they didn’t feel polished enough for it to be something I actually wanted to use daily, and so I built Yogurt to scratch that itch. I spent a lot of time fine-tuning every UI interaction/animation and optimizing the model calls to get the most out of your hardware + make it snappy. To support Windows/Mac/Linux, I decided to go with Electron. I use whisper.cpp for transcription and Apple’s on-device SpeechAnalyzer if your system supports it. For call summaries and questions, I use a local open weight LLM that automatically gets downloaded and set up based on what your hardware can handle without your cooling fans firing off like crazy (this part uses llama.cpp). I’ve spent a lot of time working on details like echo detection/reduction, global/folder/local level search respectively, and auto-end recordings. Hope this is useful for any of you who have held out on using AI note tools for privacy or cost reasons, or for folks using cloud tools who want to switch to something free and open source that still feels great to use. Would love to hear what you think about the onboarding and note taking experience :)

items.summaryZh:
嘿 HN，我是 Eric，我想分享一个我在空闲时间构建的 OSS 项目。 Yogurt 是一款获得 MIT 许可的免费桌面应用程序，它使用设备上的 AI 模型来转录、总结会议内容并进行聊天。这是一个快速演示视频：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BFfbXAwRq98 与 Granola 类似，Yogurt 在后台运行，不会加入您的通话。但与 Granola 不同的是，Yogurt 是开源、免费使用且私有的。您的会议记录、通话录音和摘要永远不会离开您的计算机。随着小型 OSS 模型变得更快、更强大，对于注重隐私和成本意识的人们来说，Yogurt 似乎是一个相当明显的胜利。您不需要前沿模型来总结会议记录或回答有关会议记录的问题。如果你想让你的笔记可供前沿模型使用，你可以直接通过 Yogurt 的本地 MCP 服务器与 Anthropic、OpenAI 等共享。无需使用付费云服务作为中间人。我尝试了一些最流行的 OSS 笔记工具，大多数都缺少日历集成、MCP 服务器等功能，或者需要您连接或创建帐户。更重要的是，它们感觉不够精致，不足以成为我真正想要每天使用的东西，所以我制作了酸奶来解决这个问题。我花了很多时间微调每个 UI 交互/动画并优化模型调用，以充分利用您的硬件并使其变得敏捷。为了支持 Windows/Mac/Linux，我决定使用 Electron。如果您的系统支持，我会使用 Whisper.cpp 进行转录，并使用 Apple 设备上的 SpeechAnalyzer。对于通话摘要和问题，我使用本地开放式权重法学硕士，它会根据您的硬件可以处理的内容自动下载和设置，而不会导致冷却风扇疯狂运转（这部分使用 llama.cpp）。我花了很多时间研究回声检测/减少、全局/文件夹/本地级别搜索以及自动结束录音等细节。希望这对那些出于隐私或成本原因而坚持使用人工智能笔记工具的人有用，或者对使用云工具但想要切换到仍然感觉很棒的免费开源工具的人有用。很想听听您对入职和笔记体验的看法:)
